blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how information travels at the speed of light through tiny glass strands? This is the magic of fibre optics!

blocks.markdown: Fibre optics is a technology that uses thin strands of glass or plastic, known as optical fibres, to transmit data as light signals. This technology relies on a principle called total internal reflection, which allows light to be guided through the fibre with minimal loss.

blocks.title: Total Internal Reflection
blocks.text: Total internal reflection occurs when a light ray travelling through a medium hits the boundary of a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, causing it to reflect entirely back into the original medium.

blocks.markdown: In fibre optics, light signals are transmitted through the core of the fibre by repeatedly bouncing off the walls, thanks to total internal reflection. This allows the light to travel long distances with very little attenuation.

blocks.title: Understanding Total Internal Reflection
blocks.prompt: Explain how total internal reflection enables light to travel through an optical fibre.

steps.text: Light enters the optical fibre at an angle greater than the critical angle.
The light reflects off the internal surface of the fibre without passing into the surrounding material.
This process repeats, allowing the light to travel through the fibre.

blocks.answer: Total internal reflection keeps the light within the fibre, allowing it to travel long distances with minimal loss.

blocks.markdown: Fibre optics has numerous applications. In medicine, optical fibres are used in endoscopes to allow doctors to view inside a patient's body without invasive surgery. In communication, they are used to transmit data over long distances with high speed and reliability.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that fibre optics is preferred over copper cables for transmitting data because it offers higher bandwidth and is less susceptible to electromagnetic interference.

points: Fibre optics relies on total internal reflection to transmit light signals.
Optical fibres are used in medicine for endoscopy and in communication for high-speed data transmission.
